title: Polymer clay skeined yarn brooch
subtitle: A brooch shaped like a miniature skein of yarn, built from polymer clay cords
excerpt: A polymer clay brooch shaped to look like a mini skein of yarn. The skein is formed by wrapping rolled polymer clay ropes into a loop and tying a contrasting colour band around the middle. The brooch pin is embedded before baking. It takes under an hour to make and no specialist equipment.
sourceNotes: Polymer clay yarn skein brooch derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling clay that cures hard at 110-130°C in a domestic oven
Kneading polymer clay by hand until warm and pliable before use

content.text: This brooch takes its shape from the look of a bundled skein of wool , the looped oval body and the contrasting tie band in the middle. The cords are made from
and mimic wrapped yarn strands. All the work is done at room temperature; baking hardens the clay.

items.name: Polymer clay, contrasting colour for the tie band

content.text: the main colour clay. Roll it into 10-12 cords, each about 3 mm in diameter and 60-70 mm long.
Bundle the cords together and bend the bundle into an oval loop , the two ends of the bundle meet at the bottom of the oval. The finished oval skein should be about 30 mm tall and 20 mm wide.
Press the cords together at both ends of the oval. Keep them separate and visible along the sides to show the yarn texture.
Add the tie band and brooch pin

Condition the contrasting colour clay. Roll a thin cord about 2 mm diameter and 30 mm long. Wrap it around the midpoint of the skein oval, over the top and around the back, and press the ends together on the back face. This represents the tie band that holds the skein together.

On the back of the skein, press the brooch pin bar into the clay while still soft. The bar should sit parallel to the tie band and be embedded far enough that it will not pull out. Add a thin clay strip over the pin bar and press it down to reinforce the fitting.
Place the brooch on a piece of baking paper on an oven tray. Bake at 130°C for 20 minutes. Allow to cool fully before handling.
The brooch is ready to wear. If the cord texture looks too smooth, sand lightly with 400-grit sandpaper and re-bake for 5 minutes to remove the sanding marks.

items.solution: Press the cords together more firmly at the bundle ends before baking. A tiny smear of liquid polymer clay at each join point also helps.

items.problem: Brooch pin comes loose after baking
items.solution: The clay over the pin bar was too thin. If it pulls loose, re-embed with two-part epoxy adhesive and clamp for 24 hours.
